question: True or false: of the ADHD studies newspapers covered most in the 1990s, most were later weakened or overturned?
answer: True. Gonon and colleagues traced the ten ADHD studies most echoed in newspapers: seven were first findings, and six of those were later refuted or much weakened. The follow-up studies got a fraction of the coverage. Papers favour the new and striking, which is just what most often fails to last.
move: Treat news of a first finding as a draft that may be rewritten.
ask: Which health story from years ago do I still believe without knowing how it turned out?
trap: False, since newspapers mostly cover studies that are well established.
reference: Gonon, Konsman, Cohen & Boraud, Why most biomedical findings echoed by newspapers turn out to be false: the case of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, PLOS ONE 7:e44275, 2012
